title: Window transparency setting (for example 0.7 opacity)
notes:
Goal: a setting that makes the app window see-through, so the desktop shows behind it at about 0.7.

Electron's options, checked against its BrowserWindow docs during the build:
- win.setOpacity(n) dims the whole window, text included, but works only on Windows and macOS. On Linux, where the user runs the app, it does nothing.
- transparent: true on the BrowserWindow (src/main/app/app-window.ts:60, which sets backgroundColor today) plus rgba backgrounds in the CSS, and xterm's allowTransparency with an rgba theme background, keeps text solid and makes only the backgrounds see-through. It works on Linux under a compositor. It is a constructor option, so changing it needs a window restart, not a live toggle.

Limits to check by hand:
- the project browser (a native WebContentsView) stays opaque;
- transparent windows have had resize, maximize and shadow problems on Windows;
- text readability over a busy wallpaper.

Proposal: one opacity setting in the settings file (1 = off) that drives the rgba backgrounds; restart to apply. Docs and a decision test for the setting's parsing, per workflow-rule-2.

comments.body: Pull request #407 opened: Window opacity setting: a see-through window behind solid text https://github.com/naeemba/dashboard/pull/407

Review loop converged in 2 rounds, ready to merge. Round 1 found 5 (1 high, 2 low, 2 nit) and fixed all 5 in 4d463d6f. The high one: every .view still painted opaque --black, so the terminals page never showed the desktop. Also: the first frame opens on the background at the chosen opacity instead of fully clear, the docs list Electron's other transparent-window limits, isWindowOpacity is no longer exported, and a test that pinned nothing was replaced with an out-of-range case. Round 2 re-review was clean. CI passed on 4d463d6f. Scope and design match the card. Still to check by hand: opacity 0.7 on Linux under a compositor, after a rebuild and restart.
